answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and puts that color's Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Each receives the Voting card set with that color on its backs, removes cards targeting colors not in play, and keeps their own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down into the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: put each ID upright in its plastic stand; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center and keep values hidden.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. After everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and choices are revealed simultaneously.

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is required. The player receiving the most votes is the Target; with Red at three and Blue and Green at two each, Red is the sole Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement, subject to the Ambush rules.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; with tied Targets, voting for any one satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, and did not play a successful Ambush. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so Red contributes no vote; Yellow votes for Red and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives and may retaliate only against a player who voted for Red, which is Yellow. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: The three-player illustration states Red's Ambush is not a vote, Red and Yellow tie as Targets, Yellow is eliminated, Red may retaliate only against Yellow, and Pink survives after voting for tied Target Yellow.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate, even if four players voted for them. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color.
answers.evidence: Ambush: the successful ambusher chooses “one of the players who voted for them”; they cannot choose someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only if its player is a Target; one played by someone who is not a Target fails and causes that player to self-eliminate.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: The round does not award gold yet. With four survivors after the vote and Ambush effects, continue with another Conspire and vote among those survivors; eliminated players do not participate in later votes that round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with three or more survivors, continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are cards whose values vary from 3 to 5 points each, not four points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. Components: each bar is a card valued at 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down; when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously and apply the payoff table.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; each chooses one face down, and both choices are revealed simultaneously when both are ready.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new bars; refill only enough to bring the pool to four.
answers.evidence: For zero survivors: each player not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Steal player receives four central Gold Bar cards and the Share player receives none.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: Share gets 0 and Steal gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Steal player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go versus Steal gives the Grab player 1 and the opponent 3; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Share player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share versus Grab One & Go gives Share 3 and Grab One & Go 1.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four, dealing them face down with values hidden.
answers.evidence: If both choose Grab One & Go, each receives one and the other two remain central; add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one Gold Bar from the deck; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of a round after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. The threshold is at least 25 points with 6–9 players and at least 24 points with 10–12 players. If several qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: check at the end of a round after bars are awarded; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 players and 24 for 10–12; the highest point total wins.

answers.answer: The tied qualifying leaders conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. If there is no winner after a round, everyone returns and IDs are stood upright for another round.

answers.answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including texting and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: discussion lasts roughly a minute and a half at most; any method is allowed, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting; the game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; target using the card matching the player's visible ID color, or play Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright so they are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: If the game continues after the entire pot is awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden. If bars remain central, deal only enough new face-down bars to bring the pool to four.
answers.evidence: Refill the central pool to four as needed; deal new central bars face down with values hidden; after the entire pot is awarded deal four, or if bars remain add only enough to bring the pool to four.

answers.answer: No. The Target is determined from the vote count, so Blue alone is the Target with four votes versus Purple's three. Blue's successful Ambush lets Blue survive but does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target and are eliminated unless a successful Ambush exception applies; Blue's survival alone does not let them survive.
answers.evidence: Vote: the player receiving the most votes is the Target; Ambush does not prevent another player from being a tied Target. Players who did not vote for any Target are eliminated, subject to successful Ambush.

answers.answer: The tie instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among three or more tied players; that procedure is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Scoring says tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary; the stated source limitation says the procedure and payoff table cover only two players and provide no arrangement for three or more tied leaders.

answers.answer: Yes. In a double-Steal extra Showdown, each player outside the two finalists receives one Gold Bar card from the deck, and that reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner. Compare totals of all players at the table after each Showdown.
answers.evidence: After each extra Showdown, compare totals of all players at the table; the one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
